summary: Implemented via Ansible (control node2 → target node1): blacklisted the usb_storage kernel module on node1 persistently and unloaded it now. ansible-core 2.20's Python-based modules are incompatible with RHEL7's python2-only interpreter (python3 not installable, no repos), so the playbook uses ansible.builtin.raw tasks over SSH to write /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-usb-storage.conf ("blacklist usb_storage" + "install usb_storage /bin/false") and unload the module if loaded. Verified module absent and explicit modprobe blocked with "Operation not permitted", both before and after a full reboot of node1. Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol for both node1 and node2, confirming new boot_id on each and full functional recovery (module still blacklisted on node1; Ansible control still works from node2).
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (RHEL7.9) and node2 (Ansible control node) baseline state; confirmed usb_storage not loaded and no yum repos available on node1
Appended node2's SSH public key to node1's antrieb user authorized_keys to enable Ansible SSH connectivity
Created inventory.ini on node2 targeting node1 with ansible_connection=ssh
Diagnosed that ansible-core 2.20's Python-based modules fail against RHEL7's python2-only interpreter and python3 cannot be installed (no repos)

Wrote blacklist-usb-storage.yml playbook using ansible.builtin.raw tasks: write /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-usb-storage.conf (blacklist + install /bin/false), unload usb_storage if loaded, verify absence
Ran the playbook successfully from node2 against node1
Verified directly on node1: module not loaded; explicit modprobe usb_storage fails with Operation not permitted
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline on node1 and node2
Restarted node1 via sudo shutdown -r now; polled until SSH returned; confirmed new boot_id
Verified post-restart on node1: blacklist config persisted, module still absent, explicit modprobe still blocked
Restarted node2 via sudo shutdown -r now; polled until SSH returned; confirmed new boot_id
Re-ran the Ansible playbook from node2 against node1 post-restart to confirm end-to-end recovery of the control workflow and persistence of the blacklist

evidence.requirement: Baseline health/state captured before any restart (node1 and node2)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id, uptime, modprobe.d content, and usb_storage load state on node1; boot_id and ansible-playbook availability on node2, prior to any restart.

evidence.requirement: usb_storage module blacklisted and unloaded now (material task outcome)
evidence.summary: Ansible playbook run from node2 wrote the modprobe.d blacklist and confirmed usb_storage absent; direct check on node1 showed module not loaded and explicit modprobe now fails with 'Operation not permitted'.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; SSH timed out mid-reboot; boot_id changed from 0d6209e2... to 987c7973...; post-restart verification shows blacklist config persisted, module absent, and modprobe still blocked.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; connection reset mid-reboot; boot_id changed from 416c5cf5... to 36fdb148...; post-restart re-run of the Ansible playbook from node2 against node1 succeeded, confirming node2's control role and node1's blacklist state both recovered.
